Start here

For most new personas, use this prompt. Replace the bracketed parts if you have them; otherwise the research will use a cross-industry default.

Create and add a persona

Recommended

Research the role, map its activities and workflows, then add it to Personas.

Create a well-researched persona for a [role] in [industry or context] and add it to Personas.

You don’t need to say “use the skill.” The persona-research method is intended to activate automatically when the request is clearly about researching or creating a persona.

Agent orientation

Before working with this system, load the orientation manifest. It gives an agent the smallest useful route through Personas, Skills, Tools, Playbooks, Docs, Decisions, and Prototyping.

Activation prompt

Recommended

Use this at the start of a session or task when the agent does not already know the system.

Use $persona-library-orientation before working with the Personas system. Load the orientation manifest, classify my request, identify the relevant space, state what you will and will not update, then proceed with the smallest useful action.
SpaceUse it forDo not use it for
PersonasRole lenses, workflows, activities, priorities, tools, skills, and evidence.Temporary experiments or broad coordination.
SkillsReusable capabilities, operating loops, quality signals, and persona applications.Tool credentials or one-off task instructions.
ToolsCapabilities, scope, permissions, availability, recipes, and lessons.Assuming access is configured or executing without authorization.
PlaybooksMulti-persona outcomes, stages, handoffs, shared state, and quality gates.Duplicating the underlying persona or skill definitions.
DocsCurrent definitions, instructions, boundaries, and examples.Unsettled alternatives or hidden history.
DecisionsDurable choices, rationale, tradeoffs, affected surfaces, and revisit conditions.Silent rewrites of the current truth.
PrototypingIsolated alternatives and persona concepts being tested.Live records or production dependencies.

Default behavior: read first, classify the request, state assumptions and scope, and remain read-only unless the requester explicitly authorizes a durable update. Finish with outcome, evidence or checks, limitations or blockers, and next action.

Create a persona

Use this when you want a new persona researched and added to Personas. You can optionally invoke the skill explicitly.

Plain-language request

Recommended

The skill should activate automatically for a clear persona request.

Create a well-researched persona for a [role] in [industry or context] and add it to Personas.

Explicit skill request

Optional

Use this when you want to make the research method unambiguous.

Use $persona-research to create a persona for a [role]. Add it to Personas.

Research only

Use this when you want the findings and synthesis but do not want the live library changed.

Research the persona of a [role] in [context]. Give me the findings only; don’t update Personas.

Update a persona

Use this to check a named source or ask for a new authoritative source. The current persona is compared with the new evidence rather than rewritten wholesale.

Check another source for [persona name], summarize what it confirms, extends, qualifies, or contradicts, and add it to the Resources section.

What changes?

Only affected claims, workflows, priorities, confidence, or open questions should be updated. The source is added with a note about what it contributes.

What you’ll get

  • Ambiguity is scopedIf a role has materially different interpretations, you’ll get a short multiple-choice question with an “Other — describe” option. Otherwise a sensible default is chosen and stated.
  • The day is mappedResearch is organized into activities, journeys, and workflows, with tools kept attached to the activities where they are used.
  • Priorities are workflow-specificThe persona shows what the person cares about most in each workflow rather than one generic list of values.
  • Capabilities are explainedThe persona identifies the skills needed to perform the work and ties them to the activities and workflows that depend on them.
  • Evidence stays visibleNew secondary-research personas are marked Working draft, with confidence, open questions, limits, and sources kept visible.

Persona skills

Use $persona-skills when you want to identify, explain, or maintain the capabilities behind a persona’s activities and workflows. It complements $persona-research: one establishes the role and its work; the other makes the skills needed to do that work explicit.

Identify needed skills

Recommended

Start with a persona and connect its skills to the work already mapped.

Use $persona-skills to identify the skills needed by this persona and connect them to its activities and workflows.

Expand one skill

Profile

Turn a capability into an evidence-backed profile with observable behavior and proficiency signals.

Use $persona-skills to expand [skill] for [persona name] into a profile with observable behaviors, tools, proficiency signals, evidence, and validation questions.

Form a reusable skill

Playbook

Use several bounded persona perspectives when the capability spans roles or needs more than one quality lens.

Use the skill formation playbook to create and integrate a reusable skill for [capability]. Have [persona 1], [persona 2], and [persona 3] contribute distinct workflows, tools, evidence, and quality signals, then use Create-skill and reconciliation.

Check a skill source

Update

Use a new source to improve only the skill claims it actually supports.

Use $persona-skills to check this source for [persona name]’s [skill] and update only what it confirms, extends, qualifies, or contradicts.

What it covers: skill definitions, related workflows, observable actions and decisions, prerequisites, tools and artifacts, failure modes, proficiency signals, evidence status, source links, and validation questions.

Persona reconciliation

Use $persona-reconciliation after adding or changing a source, claim, skill, workflow, activity, tool, or capability. It performs a scoped consistency pass so related persona content stays aligned without rewriting unrelated fields.

Reconcile a skill update

Recommended

Check the downstream effect of a new or changed capability.

Use $persona-reconciliation to review this skill change for [persona name], update affected workflows, activities, tools, priorities, needs, implications, resources, confidence, and open questions, and leave unrelated fields unchanged.

Reconcile a new source

Evidence

Classify what a source does to the current evidence before updating claims.

Use $persona-reconciliation to check this source for [persona name], classify it as confirms, extends, qualifies, or contradicts, and update only affected claims.

Reconcile a workflow change

Structure

Keep activities, tools, skills, priorities, and flow tier connected.

Use $persona-reconciliation to review this new workflow or activity for [persona name], update related skills, tools, priorities, and flow tier, and identify what remains unchanged.

What it returns: a scoped update set, checked unchanged fields, evidence and confidence changes, resource entries, and open questions. It is the shared final pass called by $persona-research and $persona-skills; use it directly when you already know what changed.

Persona panel orchestration

Use $persona-panel-orchestration when you want one or more named personas to assess a question, artifact, draft, or decision. The skill processes each selected persona independently, compares their perspectives, and returns a concise synthesis.

Consult one persona

Single lens

Use one persona’s workflows, skills, priorities, and evidence as the primary lens.

Use $persona-panel-orchestration with [persona name] to help me [goal]. Return a recommendation, relevant quality signals, risks, evidence, and next actions.

Assemble a panel

Multiple lenses

Name two to four personas with distinct perspectives; the skill keeps their independent judgments visible before synthesizing.

Use $persona-panel-orchestration with [persona 1], [persona 2], and [persona 3] to review [artifact or question]. Synthesize the recommendation and preserve disagreements, assumptions, evidence, and next actions.

Run a playbook

Coordinated workflow

Use a named playbook when the work needs stages, handoffs, decision rights, shared state, or quality gates.

Use $persona-panel-orchestration with the [playbook name] playbook to help me [goal]. Show the current stage, participant perspectives, evidence gaps, and next action.
  • You choose the participantsThe first version does not automatically select or invent a meta-persona. If the choice materially changes the result, you’ll get a bounded question with concrete options.
  • Each perspective stays groundedThe skill uses the persona’s workflows, skills, priorities, sources, confidence, and open questions rather than theatrical role-play.
  • The synthesis is not a silent updateIt can offer Save as Draft, Propose Decision, Add to Docs, or Create Playbook Artifact, but durable changes require an explicit request.

Default response: recommendation, why, persona perspectives, agreement and disagreement, assumptions and confidence, then the smallest useful next action.

Tool discovery and safe execution

Use $tool-discovery-and-safe-execution when work needs a new tool, connector, MCP, repository, document space, design file, or local workspace. It resolves the smallest capability, names the workspace and permission boundary, runs a safe probe, and records what can be learned.

Resolve a capability

Recommended

Ask the skill to find the safest available tool without hard-coding a vendor into the persona.

Use $tool-discovery-and-safe-execution to resolve the safest available tool for [capability] within [workspace or scope], and return the proposed action, permission, fallback, and verification method.

Adopt a new tool or MCP

Onboarding

Use this when the capability is not yet mapped or a new connector needs a safe first test.

Use $tool-discovery-and-safe-execution to assess [tool or MCP] for [capability]. Run a read-only or sandboxed probe, document its limits, and do not grant new permissions or make shared changes.
  • Capability before vendorRequest inspect, search, prototype, edit, verify, or publish first; resolve the actual tool second.
  • Scope before actionName the file, repository, folder, page, branch, or local path and the exact permission before using it.
  • Evidence before learningOne run creates a usage note. Shared guidance requires review, repeated evidence, or explicit approval.

Default response: outcome, required capability, selected tool and connector, workspace, permission and approval status, action or blocker, verification evidence, usage-record status, lesson status, and next action.

Tool record maintenance

Use $tool-record-maintenance when the canonical Tools catalog needs a new record, field update, relationship, reconciliation, audit, or retirement. It maintains documentation and relationships; it does not configure access or execute a connector.

Add or update a record

Catalog

Describe the change while preserving scope, availability, evidence, and revision history.

Use $tool-record-maintenance to [add or update] the [tool or MCP] record. Include capabilities, scope, risk, permissions, fallbacks, availability status, related personas, skills, playbooks, recipes, evidence, and revision history. Do not execute the tool or change access.

Reconcile overlapping tools

Architecture

Use this when two records may describe the same capability or have different boundaries.

Use $tool-record-maintenance to reconcile [tool record A] and [tool record B]. Compare identity, capability, connector, scope, risk, evidence, and relationships, then recommend merge, preserve, supersede, or keep both.
  • Record is not availabilityA tool record explains what could be used; the requester’s exposed tools determine what is actually available now.
  • Recipe is not a new core skillKeep portable judgment in Skills and tool-specific procedures in recipes linked from the Tool record.
  • Maintenance is not executionUse $tool-discovery-and-safe-execution separately when a safe probe or real tool action is needed.

Persona prototypes

Use a prototype persona when you want to test a role concept without changing the live Personas library. A prototype can reference existing personas, skills, tools, and workflows, but live records must not depend on it until it passes a promotion gate.

Test a persona concept

Isolated

Run representative conversations without changing Personas, Skills, or Playbooks.

Create a prototype persona for [concept]. Keep it isolated from the live Personas library. Define its assumptions, workflows, skills, tools, quality signals, test scenarios, and open questions. Do not update existing records.

Evaluate promotion

After testing

Use evidence from representative scenarios before deciding whether the prototype should become live.

Evaluate prototype persona [name] against [test scenarios]. Preserve disagreements and open questions. Recommend archive, continue testing, or promote, and if promoting list the affected Personas, Skills, Tools, Playbooks, Docs, and Decisions.

Boundary: prototype records use a proto-persona- ID, remain outside live counts and catalogs, and move to the live system only through an explicit Decisions record followed by reconciliation.

Persona Library Guide

Use the Persona Library Guide when a new LLM needs to enter the system without loading every record at once. It is an onboarding and routing persona: it prepares a grounded handoff to the relevant persona, skill, tool, or playbook.

Bootstrap a new LLM

Recommended

Give the new model the system map, request classification, and safe mutation boundary before asking it to do substantive work.

Consult the Persona Library Guide. Read the orientation manifest, classify my request, identify the smallest relevant space and records, assemble the minimum context packet, state assumptions and permission boundaries, then give me the recommended persona or skill invocation. Do not update anything.
Guide outputWhat it provides
ClassificationAnswer, research, plan, prototype, consult, or authorized update.
RoutingThe smallest relevant space and record types.
Context packetGoal, artifacts, constraints, capabilities, permissions, and success criteria.
HandoffA precise prompt for the selected persona, skill, tool recipe, or playbook.
Safety boundaryWhat is unavailable, read-only, prototype-only, or explicitly authorized.
Prerequisite gateAfter an output is selected, re-check required inputs. Offer a bounded choice between providing missing materials and creating a placeholder template.

Do not bypass missing evidence: selecting “full packet” chooses the desired output, not permission to invent or imply tailored content. The guide should preserve the choice, identify blocking inputs, and offer the smallest safe next step.

Prototype status: the guide is being tested separately in Prototyping. It becomes a live Persona only after representative routing tests and an explicit Decisions record.

Change-impact reconciliation

Use $change-impact-reconciliation when new evidence, a record, a decision, a prototype promotion, or a generated artifact changes. It checks downstream effects so stale placeholders, assumptions, and contradictory claims do not survive a source update.

Run a reconciliation pass

After changes

Use this after adding a source or updating a durable record. It is read-only unless the request explicitly authorizes a write.

Use $change-impact-reconciliation after this change. Identify affected records and artifacts, classify each impact as confirms, extends, qualifies, contradicts, invalidates, or unrelated, update only affected fields, scan for stale placeholders and assumptions, validate downstream outputs, and return blockers, confidence, revision summary, and next action. Do not make durable changes unless I authorize them.
SpaceReconciliation check
PersonasWorkflows, activities, skills, tools, priorities, resources, confidence, and open questions.
SkillsOperating loop, quality signals, triggers, evidence, persona applications, and related capabilities.
ToolsCapability availability, permission scope, recipes, fallbacks, and lessons learned.
PlaybooksStages, prerequisites, handoffs, shared state, artifacts, and quality gates.
DocsCurrent truth, links, navigation, boundaries, and prototype-versus-live labels.
Generated artifactsSource traceability, stale placeholders, duplicate or contradictory content, and completion status.

Working rule: a skill-specific workflow does the research or update; reconciliation checks what that work changed elsewhere. An unrelated or unchanged result is valid when the review finds no material downstream effect.

Test the reconciliation prototype →Read the persona-specific adapter →

Conditional skill contract

Every skill declares how its work can change the system. That declaration lets a lower-reasoning model route the reconciliation step consistently without running it for every read-only consultation.

Change modeDefault handoff
read_onlySkip reconciliation unless the skill creates a durable artifact or an impact review is requested.
prototypeCheck isolation and live-record leakage only; prototype content is not live truth.
source_update, record_update, artifact_generationInvoke $change-impact-reconciliation before the final handoff.
external_executionInvoke it when the execution creates a durable usage record, lesson, recipe, or artifact.
reconciliation_adapterRun the domain adapter first, then one universal pass without recursion.

Author a new skill

Contract

Declare these fields in the skill frontmatter. They route behavior; they never grant permission to write.

When creating or updating a skill, declare metadata: change_mode, change_domain, and reconciliation. If the mode is source_update, record_update, artifact_generation, or applicable external_execution, invoke $change-impact-reconciliation before handoff. If it is read_only, skip it unless a durable artifact is created. If it is prototype, check isolation only. Keep all reconciliation read-only unless I explicitly authorize a durable update.

Important: automatic means “part of the skill’s default process,” not a hidden runtime scheduler. A skill without metadata falls back to read-only behavior and reports the missing contract.

Prototyping

Use $layout-lab when the information architecture is unsettled and you want to compare real structures before changing the main experience. Prototyping is the active working space: it creates a throwaway comparison surface and keeps the sample content constant. Once a direction is chosen, archive the rationale in Decisions before applying it to the Site or product surface.

Explore options

Recommended

Ask for a small set of materially different structures using the same content.

Use $layout-lab to show me three ways to organize [content or workflow] before changing the main page. Keep the sample content constant and explain the tradeoffs.

Apply a choice

After selection

Carry the chosen direction through the live page and any related documentation.

I choose Option [A–F]. Use $layout-lab to apply it to the main page, update any related skill or Docs page, and record the decision.

Good labs compare structure, not decoration. Keep the lab available as an exploration, make the chosen direction obvious, and record what remains open for validation.

Source updates

A persona can be strengthened over time. When you ask for another source, the current evidence is compared with the new evidence instead of being overwritten wholesale.

ResultMeaning
ConfirmsThe new source supports an existing claim or workflow.
ExtendsThe new source adds a useful responsibility, constraint, or priority.
QualifiesThe new source narrows the claim or adds an important condition.
ContradictsThe new source conflicts with the current synthesis and may lower confidence or create an open question.

Use this exact request

Ask me to check a named source or find an authoritative one, explain what it contributes, and add it to the persona’s Resources section.

The mental model

The site has reusable knowledge layers and separate working-record layers. Each has one job, so larger workflows can compose existing material without turning every use case into a new kind of record.

LayerWhat it answers
PersonaWho is operating, in what lifecycle, context, and state?
Persona tool requirementWhich capability does an activity need, what is the preferred path, and what is the safe fallback?
SkillWhat portable capability is needed, and how can quality be recognized?
Tool-use recipeHow is that capability performed for a specific task in a specific tool?
Persona workflowHow does that person perform a meaningful flow of activities?
PlaybookHow do several personas, skills, recipes, workflows, artifacts, and gates coordinate toward an outcome?
Tool recordWhat capability, scope, access path, permission, fallback, and evidence does a tool provide?
PrototypingWhich structure or interaction direction should be tested before it becomes current?
DecisionWhat choice is durable, why was it made, and what does it affect?

Keep the distinction clear: personas are lenses, skills are portable capabilities, tool-use recipes make capabilities practical, workflows describe how a persona works, and playbooks coordinate reusable material toward an outcome.

Docs, Prototyping, and Decisions

Use the three spaces together without making them duplicate each other. Prototyping is active experimentation, Decisions preserve selected choices, and Docs explain the current system.

SpacePrimary questionKeep here
DocsWhat is true now, and how do I use it?Definitions, boundaries, instructions, examples, prompts, and the current information architecture.
PrototypingWhat could this become, and which direction works best?Alternative structures, interaction directions, sample content, and temporary comparison surfaces.
DecisionsWhy was this direction chosen, what changed, and when should we revisit it?Selected options, alternatives considered, tradeoffs, evidence, status, affected surfaces, and revisit conditions.

Working rule: Prototyping explores. Decisions archive. Docs contain the current truth. Link a prototype to its decision record, and link the decision back to the Docs section or product surface it changed.

  • Use Docs for orientationSomeone should be able to learn the system or complete a task without reading the entire history.
  • Use Prototyping for comparisonKeep alternatives visible while the structure is unsettled, without implying that any option is current truth.
  • Use Decisions for trustSomeone should be able to understand the tradeoff, see what was applied, and know what could cause the choice to change.
  • Keep one canonical explanationDo not copy whole sections between spaces. Point from the current Docs rule to its decision record when context matters.

Status flows

Prototypes move Active → Selected → Archived. Decisions move Proposed → Decided → Applied → Superseded. Use Parked for a useful idea intentionally deferred.

Composed playbooks

A playbook is larger than one persona or skill. It defines stages, participants, handoffs, decision rights, shared state, quality gates, and a learning loop. It calls existing personas and skills rather than copying them.

  • PrimitivesPersonas, skills, resources, tools, artifacts, and persona-owned workflows.
  • CompositionStages, routing, handoffs, decision rights, quality gates, and flow dependencies.
  • InstanceThe user’s actual goal, constraints, evidence, artifact versions, decisions, and feedback.

Current example

Evidence-led job search coordinates role calibration, evidence mapping, ATS review, human narrative, visual communication, outreach, interviews, and learning.

Create and integrate a reusable skill coordinates a boundary-setting persona, relevant domain personas, an orchestrator, Create-skill, and reconciliation.

Open the skill formation playbook →

Skill boundary: playbooks coordinate the work, while Multi-perspective skill synthesis captures the reusable reasoning inside the process. A broader playbooks skill can later standardize outcome framing, stage decomposition, routing, shared state, gates, handoffs, and reconciliation across multiple playbooks.

Application context and reviews

The context brief describes one application. The Site holds reusable skills and coordination guidance. Give the brief and original sources to the agent when invoking the evidence-led job-search playbook.

  • SkillsPreserve evidence, shape specific writing, judge density, and inspect document quality. Authored guidance is distinct from starter scaffolding and is not proof of tested outcomes.
  • PersonasLeah applies source-preserving editing and separate ATS/human reviews; Sofia applies content shaping, page judgment, and production review.
  • PlaybooksCoordinate the brief, claim ledger, small content trial, artifact versions, independent findings, disagreements, and reconciliation.
  • DocsExplain the current process, inputs, prompts, review statuses, and tool limitations.
  • PrototypingKeep trial content and layout comparisons isolated until a direction is selected. The editorial trial is ready to run.
  • DecisionsPreserve the chosen process and its rationale. Read the document evidence and quality decision.

Bring the minimum useful context

Include the reader and goal, original career sources, target description and access/completeness status, proposed positioning, deliverables, constraints, source versions, and unresolved questions. Keep candidate facts and target-specific findings in this working brief. Reference the Site’s shared methods rather than copying them into every application.

Keep the handoff explicit

Read brief and originals → map claims → trial the content → produce the requested document → run independent reviews → reconcile. Use the requester’s available tools and scoped workspace. If a tool or source is missing, identify the affected check early and continue useful work that does not depend on it.

Verdicts: Pass means the criterion was checked on the named version; Revise identifies an observed weakness; Blocked names a missing prerequisite; Not reviewed means the check has not run. Record the source/passage or page, finding, reader consequence, action, and limitation. A checklist is not a completed review.

Start the small editorial trial

Draft only
Use the evidence-led job-search playbook with the existing job-search council and Sofia Calder. Read my attached context brief, original career sources, and target description. Build a traceable claim ledger and draft only a summary and two role entries. Review each perspective independently. Preserve disagreements and source meaning. Report version-specific findings and limitations. Do not create a full resume, update the Site, or submit anything.

Personas behavior

When a persona is added to Personas, the site keeps the browsing model simple and the detail view deep.

  • Top levelBrowse and filter by role group, such as Operators, Leaders, or Specialists.
  • Persona detailSee lifecycle, operating context, operating state, activities, tools, skills, journeys, and flow hierarchy.
  • SkillsBrowse reusable capabilities across personas, then open a skill to inspect triggers, observable practice, workflows, and evidence.
  • Revision historyReview the semantic record of what changed and which evidence or confidence supported the change.
  • ResourcesFind the cited source trail at the end of the persona detail, after revision history and the product implication.
